style_when: the story is a product, a device, a price or a market for a thing the reader could buy — an appliance, a panel, a router, a robot arm
prompt: Editorial product photograph: a compact unbranded build-runner workstation tower — matte polymer chassis, brushed steel faceplate, one small safety-yellow status LED — standing on sealed concrete at the edge of a data hall, a dark rack row blurred far behind it. A single softbox key light rakes in low from the left, its soft directional falloff throwing a cast shadow many times the box's own length, stretching right across the empty graphite floor. Extreme asymmetric 16:9 framing: the box low in the left third, vast negative space above the long shadow. 35mm lens, moderate depth of field, fine film grain, cool graphite and bone-white palette. No people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, printed numbers, watermark, logo
rationale: The story turns on the price of a purchasable machine — the runner or workstation box that pays itself back in weeks — so a product treatment is the honest match, provided it sits in a material world. One low raking key light makes the $2.94 box cast the $77.94 shadow: the machine barely shows, and the long dark mass carries the bill. studio_object is unused in the recent set, keeping the desk varied after isometric, telephoto, cinematic and flat-lay.
cue: the wait is billed as salary
subject: an unbranded build-runner workstation tower casting a shadow far longer than itself
core_thesis: A build's true cost is billed in salary, not machine time — GitHub's 92-minute build cost $81 total, of which only $2.94 was compute and $77.94 was the developer's waiting time, a 26.5x payroll multiple.
core_conflict: Cheap visible machine minutes ($2.94 of compute on an 8-core runner) against the invisible payroll of interrupted attention ($77.94 of developer time plus a 23-minute re-entry tax per wait)
composition: Extreme asymmetric 16:9: the runner box small and low in the left third, its long shadow raking right across the empty floor, blurred rack row behind, generous negative space above

review.depicts: A small dark unbranded computer tower standing low in the left third of a polished concrete floor, casting a long shadow raking to the right, with a blurred row of server racks and ceiling lights in the background and empty space above.
review.reason: The frame depicts the article's own protagonist — a build-runner tower whose shadow far exceeds its size, matching the story's mechanism that machine time is tiny relative to the waiting cost it imposes.
